searchText: turbogeth? 😆 correct answer 🙂 Does that address the underlying issue or just increase overall performance such that it doesn't matter (brute force solution to the problem)? If the latter, I worry that won't help since if TurboGeth's strategy becomes widely adopted then people will want to increase block gas limits and we'll be right back in the same situation with mispricing. it increases performance of the operations that form the core of those exploits I see, so TG's performance benefits are focused (conveniently) in areas that these problems are present. Yes, it will help, because the point at which the vulnerability starts will be much higher > turbogeth Also, geth with `--snapshot` enabled Besu is also working on a similar DB format (<@!403707149043105803> named it Bonsai Tries 🙂 ) which should help us deal with these types of operations more efficiently. very interesting
